text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- RECORD SALES OF CONSTRUCTION MATERIAL
After showing a record volume of $21 billion in 1996, construction firms expect sales to be even higher this year.
-- BOLSAS HAVE A GOOD START IN 1997

Brazilian bolsas rose on strong volume, boosted by a rise on Wall Street, hopes over the approval of a re-election amendment and expectations that foreign investors in stocks will be exempt from a new financial tax.
-- LATIN AMERICA RAISED $87 BLN IN 1996
Latin American countries raised a record $87.6 billion in the international capital markets in 1996. Mexico, Argentina and Brazil led the bond issues.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- GOV'T SPEEDS UP RE-ELECTION AGENDA
The federal government decided to speed up the votes on a constitutional amendment which will give President Fernando Henrique Cardoso the chance for running for a second term.

A special lower house committee will vote on the re-election amendment on January 13. The amendment will go for a first vote on the floor of the Chamber of Deputies on January 15, and for a second vote on January 22.
-- DEATH TOLL CAUSED BY RAINS IN MINAS RISE TO 70
Seventy people died because of torrential rainfall in Minas Gerais state. The federal government said it will grant emergency funds to the state.
O GLOBO
-- RIO SETS PLAN AGAINST SUMMER RAINS
Rio de Janeiro mayor office announces plan to protect the city from summer rains. On Monday, Civil Defense officials began to notify 700 families that live in risky areas.
-- LANDLESS MOVEMENT CHALLENGES THE GOV'T AND OCCUPY FARMS
The Landless Movement (MST) led the invasion by 1,200 families of five farms in Pontal do Paranapanema in Sao Paulo state.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511-2485412))
